metadata.description: declarative checking vs real QEC re-computation practices (Gap 6), de-circularised
metadata.pythonhashseed: 0 via main() self re-exec (QUITS circuit text is hash-seed dependent; metrics are not)

source_faithful.read_sets: auto-extracted from the pinned QUITS tree by experiments/extract_read_sets.py (READ_SETS_FROM_SOURCE)
source_faithful.edges: auto-derived: ARTIFACT_READS_FROM_SOURCE minus self-loops (ASSEMBLY_EDGES_FROM_SOURCE): extractor <- code, arch <- code, decoder <- (code, extractor)
source_faithful.faithfulness: faithful by construction (AST-extracted), cross-validated against the dynamic measurements in experiments/dynamic_impact.json

methodology.anti_circularity: The previous version of this experiment defined the checker's prediction as 'recompute everything that could be affected' and reported 0 misses by construction.  Here ground truth (byte-level artifact fingerprints per step) is measured independently on the pinned QUITS tree; each strategy's rebuild set is predicted from declared information only — for the checker, the declared read sets R(c) and the artifact-DAG edges via semantics.coordinate_impact — and scored against ground truth only afterwards.  predict_checker/predict_config_diff/predict_logbook/predict_declarative_naive/predict_declarative_omniscient take specs (plus the logged intent), never the fingerprint table; this is enforced by their signatures and locked by experiments/test_practice_comparison.py.  The omniscient declarative variant uses the same declared-information channel as the checker (the source-faithful read sets), never the measured fingerprints — it models a user whose declarations happen to be perfect, not a peek at the answer.
methodology.declarative_vs_config_diff: config_diff and declarative_naive are NOT the same practice. config_diff has no declarations at all: it diffs the spec file and rebuilds the artifacts of whatever dimension changed, so (i) it cannot attach different dependencies to different artifacts of one component and (ii) it knows nothing about artifact-file wiring, missing e.g. the decoder's consumption of the circuit.  declarative_naive declares per-artifact dependencies and the pipeline-visible file edges, and make's cascade closes exactly those pipeline-level misses.  What no declaration at the pipeline interface can express is a coordinate read hidden INSIDE a component call — extractor -> noise (H3) enters build_circuit as a parameter value, not as a file, so the file DAG has no edge for it and every declarative-build user, however honest, keeps the extractor's circuit/DEM/predictions stale on noise-only steps.  declarative_omniscient is the upper bound in which the declared coordinate sets are the true ones: it reaches the checker's prediction, showing the checker's information content equals perfect declarations.

declarative_naive_declaration_sets.omitted_hidden_read: extractor -> noise (H3): inside build_circuit, not a pipeline file

metrics.missed: artifact changed by ground truth but not rebuilt (the dangerous case: stale artifact in use)
metrics.over_rebuilds: artifact rebuilt but byte-identical (wasted compute, not incorrect)
metrics.wall_clock_est_s: builds x calibration seconds per build kind

strategies.full_rerun: rebuild every artifact at every step (cost baseline)
strategies.config_diff: 'git diff the config': rebuild only artifacts of dimensions whose declared spec value changed; runtime reads invisible; no per-artifact declarations at all (pure spec-file diff)
strategies.declarative_naive: make/snakemake practice, honest user: per-artifact declarations binding each artifact to its nominal component coordinate + pipeline-visible artifact-file edges (ASSEMBLY_EDGES_FROM_SOURCE) + make-style cascade; the runtime read extractor->noise (H3) happens inside build_circuit, has no file edge, and is therefore un-declarable
strategies.declarative_omniscient: same declaration mechanism, but declared coordinate sets are the true impact closure (extractor->noise included): the upper bound of what any declarative-build user can reach
strategies.logbook: manual lab notebook: rebuild only the intent dimension's artifacts; all cross-dimension staleness missed
strategies.checker: our tool: declared read sets R(c) + artifact-DAG cone (coordinate_impact on the source-faithful assembly); prediction uses no ground truth

methodology.reproducibility: Ground truth is byte-level, so every step must decode reproducibly.  The SD6-10x noise setting is excluded from the log because at that saturated operating point both QUITS decoders give different outputs on identical inputs across calls (unseeded randomness inside ldpc's OSD/LSD tie-breaking); SD6 / SI1000 / SD6-0.1x are verified deterministic for both decoders on every code family used.
methodology.expected_outcome: checker misses 0 on the QUITS model because R(extractor) already contains noise (H3); config_diff, logbook and declarative_naive miss the extractor's circuit/DEM/predictions on every noise-only step — the measured blind spot of both the git-diff practice and (identically, on those steps) the honest declarative-build practice, since the extractor->noise read is not declarable at the file interface.  declarative_naive still closes every miss caused by pipeline-visible coupling (its file edges catch the decoder's consumption of the circuit and the layout's consumption of the code), so it strictly improves on config_diff on the extractor-swap and code-port steps while paying almost nothing in over-rebuilds.  declarative_omniscient matches the checker's prediction: perfect declarations = the checker's information content.
